what: The tuned-TCP baseline sweep: max_concurrency x parts_in_flight on four link profiles, the untuned default beside it, confirmation runs of the best-tuned point, and contended rows. Raw data: runs.csv (one row per run), objects.csv (one row per batch/object), cycles.csv (one row per process-once), sweep_index.csv (every attempt, refusals included), host_noise.csv, rq4_presence.csv. Derived: points.csv, gate.json, measurements_table.md here, and the charts in docs/assets/egress-483/ - all regenerated by `python3 benchmarks/egress_baseline.py report --data <this dir> --charts docs/assets/egress-483`.

host.shared_with: Docker Desktop and its unrelated containers (about ten, other projects), other sessions' work inside Docker Desktop, the stopped VMs of other projects, and from 01:06:58Z on 2026-11-11 another session's Kafka/MinIO benchmark (rq4). None of it was stopped.

noise_samplers.host_noise.csv: a shell loop on the Mac: sysctl vm.loadavg and the idle percentage of `top -l 2`, then sleep 28 s; observed cadence 30-35 s (median 31 s), 22:44Z to 02:29Z. 29 of 432 rows read exactly 0.0% idle, several at a load average of 7-10; these look like failed parses of top's output rather than saturation and are excluded from the doc's mean (45.5% idle without them, 42.5% with). rustc_procs/cargo_procs count macOS processes named rustc/cargo and read 0 throughout: builds run inside Docker Desktop's VM are not visible to them, so these columns show nothing about other sessions' builds.
noise_samplers.rq4_presence.csv: `docker ps --filter name=rq4` (read-only) every 30 s from 01:09:30Z on 2026-11-11. The first row, 01:06:58Z, is the rq4 containers' creation time from `docker ps`, which at 01:09:16Z showed them up for two minutes; collect --busy treats the span from that row to the first sampled row as occupied, so the first 152 s are the containers' uptime, not sampled. Every sample after it saw the containers running, to the last run.

lab_vms.roles: a and b: one grid repetition each on the two 100 ms profiles, then confirmation and contended runs; c: the clean-LAN grid and the policed rows; d (added when the policed rows proved slow): the default's confirmation runs, then confirmation and contended runs
lab_vms.why_several: parallel repetitions: the 100 ms profiles are link-bound at 10 Mbit/s, so a VM per repetition cuts wall time without making any one run CPU-bound; every run is still gated on its own calibration
lab_vms.hypervisor: Lima 2.3.0, vz, 6 vCPU, 8 GiB, 40 GiB disk each; vCPUs are not pinned to host cores (vz does not expose that), so 'a pinned core' is not available on this platform
lab_vms.guest: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-142-generic, Docker 29.9.3, Compose v5.7.0
lab_vms.ifb: available (modprobe ifb succeeds), so the middlebox runs exactly as lib/netem.py builds it: policer on the engine-facing ingress hook, upload impairment and bottleneck on the ifb. No egress-shaping substitute was used.

engine_binary.name: vtopctl 0.7.0
engine_binary.source: origin/main 3564edc (the branch changes no engine code)
engine_binary.built_with: rust:latest (rustc 1.99.1) in Docker inside vtop-bench-483a, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, cargo build --release --locked --no-default-features --bin vtopctl; the same file copied to the other three VMs (sha256 checked on each)
engine_binary.why_no_default_features: the only default feature is the Kafka source adapter, which links libsasl2; the lab engine image (ubuntu:26.04) has no libsasl2. The file source, batching and the s3_native path measured here do not depend on it.

harness: benchmarks/egress_baseline.py run -> benchmarks/run_benchmark.py, run directly on each VM (python 3.12, PyYAML), runner_mode container, the netem + containerized compose profiles. Engine and store CPU from the containers' cgroup v2 cpu.stat around each run. The contended rows numbered 11 ran on the harness after this branch merged main 7472b64 (#531, its fix to the competitor's window placement); every other run on the harness before it.
sweep_index_run_id: a blank run_id marks an attempt the harness refused before it created a run directory, so there is nothing to trace it to; each such row is identified by its vm and started_utc, which are unique. Later sweeps also write an attempt_id column.
workload: one whole 20 MiB JSONL file per batch (whole_file, batch_max_records 1), compression none, sha256, s3_native to the lab MinIO through the middlebox (netem:9200). Backlog max(4, 2 x max_concurrency) objects per run on the shaped profiles, 64 on the clean LAN; the default's width is eight, so 16. Part size 5 MiB on grid points (four parts per object); the default keeps 8 MiB parts and four in flight. Contended rows: scenario 18's workload with only the width replaced.

links.lan: the middlebox in the path, no qdisc
links.wan100: netem 100 ms round trip (50 ms each way), no jitter, no loss, tbf 10000 kbit/s at 1.0 BDP (125000 bytes)
links.wan100-loss1: wan100 plus 1% gemodel loss (mean burst two packets) on the upload direction only
links.wan100-policed: netem 100 ms round trip, a 10000 kbit/s policer on the ingress hook (5000-byte bucket), no tbf and no queue
